title: Scammers target hundreds of thousands of crypto owners after Trezor confirms data breach of email provider
slides: Trezor data breach: are your crypto funds safe?
Scammers now have emails from hundreds of thousands
But threat goes beyond phishing: SIM swaps
Never reuse your email for exchanges
Check haveibeenpwned today; move funds if needed
thread_text:
1. The breach that follows you

Hundreds of thousands of Trezor users had their emails exposed. Even if your crypto is safe, your inbox is now a target.

2. Your email is the key

Attackers use that address to try password resets on exchanges. One reused login and they're inside.

3. Beyond phishing emails

With your phone number, they can SIM-swap your line and intercept two-factor codes. Your funds are one step away.

4. The tiny mistake that costs everything

If you used the same email for exchanges and newsletters, attackers now have a direct map to your accounts.

5. Check if you're exposed

Go to haveibeenpwned.com and enter your email. If it shows up, move your funds to a new wallet today.

instagram.caption:
Hundreds of thousands of Trezor users just had their emails handed to scammers. 🚨

The breach didn't touch your crypto directly — it exposed the address tied to your account.

If you reused that email for an exchange login, attackers can now try password resets on it.

Some go further: with your phone number, a SIM swap lets them intercept your two-factor codes. 📱

For anyone building in crypto or posting about it, that email is now a map back to your funds.

Go check haveibeenpwned.com right now. If your address shows up, move your funds today.
